questions.q: Why does the lesson describe infrastructure without naming conventions as a 'silent' failure mode?
options: Because it immediately crashes the cluster with a loud error
Because it degrades usability gradually (unclear job names, overwritten checkpoints) without ever throwing an error
Because it only affects audio logging systems
Because it is caused by researchers deliberately hiding their work
questions.explain: Generic job names, untagged runs, and overwritten checkpoints don't produce errors -- they just make the shared infrastructure progressively harder to use until someone has to reconstruct what should have been obvious.

questions.q: What problem does an explicit checkpoint retention policy solve?
options: It makes training run faster by reducing disk I/O
It prevents both silently running out of shared storage and disputes over someone deleting a file another person still needed
It automatically improves model accuracy
It eliminates the need for experiment tracking entirely
questions.explain: Without an agreed rule, teams either silently exhaust shared storage quota or face conflict when someone manually deletes a checkpoint another person assumed was safe -- an explicit policy (e.g. keep best+latest, delete after 30 days unless tagged) avoids both.

questions.q: What is the actual test the lesson proposes for whether a team's shared-infrastructure conventions are working?
options: Whether the cluster has 100% uptime
Whether a new team member can be productive in a day rather than a week of asking around
Whether the team has the most GPUs of any lab
Whether every job finishes successfully on the first try
questions.explain: The lesson frames the real test as onboarding speed: conventions only work if they're written down discoverably (e.g. an INFRASTRUCTURE.md) rather than living only in the memory of whoever originally set things up.

questions.q: What does a consistent job-naming convention like `<project>-<experiment>-<trial-or-seed>` cost a researcher to follow, and what does it buy the team?
options: It costs significant extra compute and buys faster training
It costs essentially nothing extra to follow and buys a navigable, filterable shared cluster as job counts grow
It costs a separate software license and buys GPU priority
It costs extra storage and buys faster checkpoint loading
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that a naming convention is nearly free to follow but prevents job names like job1 or test from piling up unreadably in a shared queue.

questions.q: What four things does the lesson suggest a team's INFRASTRUCTURE.md should document?
options: The CEO's biography, company history, funding rounds, and office locations
How to request cluster access/QoS, naming conventions, where shared datasets live and how to version them, and the storage retention policy
Only the GPU model numbers used in the cluster
A list of every researcher's personal email address
questions.explain: The lesson specifically lists: cluster access and partition/QoS to use, job/tracking naming conventions, shared dataset locations and versioning, and the storage retention policy as the core content of a discoverable infrastructure doc.
